## R Markdown
```{r}
## Overview

This R Markdown file documents the analysis of astrocytes from previously published
mouse cortical single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data attributed to Zhou et al. (2020),
comparing WT and 5xFAD conditions at approximately 7 months of age.

**Public data source:** Zhou et al., GEO accession [GSE140510](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE140510), 7-month mouse single-nucleus RNA-seq. The analysis uses three WT and three 5xFAD biological replicates (WT1–WT3 and FAD1–FAD3). The downloaded, processed 10x-format count matrices were placed in six corresponding sample folders. Each folder contains `barcodes.tsv.gz`, `features.tsv.gz`, and `matrix.mtx.gz`. In the original local preparation, prefixes were removed from the downloaded filenames to make them compatible with `Read10X()`.

**Input layout:** Place this R Markdown file alongside a `data/` directory containing the six sample folders (or edit `data_dir` below). The raw FASTQ files are **not** needed for this workflow; this analysis starts with the processed count matrices supplied by the original study. This R Markdown now reproduces preparation of the combined starting Seurat object, previously saved as `7m_snRNAseq_combined.rds`.

**Original analytical choices retained:** QC (200–7000 detected genes,
500–50000 counts, up to 15% mitochondrial reads); per-sample decontX;
removal of cells with estimated contamination above 0.30; per-sample
scDblFinder singlet selection; Harmony correction by sample; graph clustering
at resolution 0.3; astrocyte subset from cluster 8; CXCL14-positive status
based on at least one corrected RNA count.

**Note:** Cluster numbers and gene-expression plots depend on software versions
and upstream preprocessing. The identity of cluster 8 as astrocytes was
established by inspecting established astrocyte markers in the original run.
```

```{r}
## 1. Load public processed count matrices and assemble the starting Seurat object

The six 10x count matrices are read individually to retain sample identity and genotype, then merged into the starting Seurat object. This step replaces the original in-memory lookup `get("7m_snRNAseq_combined")` and avoids a machine-specific `setwd()` path.

```{r libraries-and-input}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(Seurat)
  library(dplyr)
  library(Matrix)
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
  library(celda)
  library(scDblFinder)
  library(harmony)
  library(ggplot2)
})

# Expected directories: data/WT1, data/WT2, data/WT3,
#                       data/FAD1, data/FAD2, data/FAD3.
data_dir <- "data"
sample_table <- data.frame(
  folder = c("WT1", "WT2", "WT3", "FAD1", "FAD2", "FAD3"),
  sample_id = c("WT1", "WT2", "WT3", "FAD1", "FAD2", "FAD3"),
  condition = c(rep("WT", 3), rep("5XFAD", 3)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

load_sample <- function(folder_name, sample_id, condition) {
  path <- file.path(data_dir, folder_name)
  expected_files <- file.path(path, c("barcodes.tsv.gz", "features.tsv.gz", "matrix.mtx.gz"))
  if (!all(file.exists(expected_files))) {
    stop("Missing 10x matrix file(s) in ", path,
         ". See the input folder layout above.")
  }
  counts <- Read10X(data.dir = path)
  s <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts, project = sample_id)
  s$sample_id <- sample_id
  s$condition <- condition
  s
}

sample_objects <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(sample_table)), function(i) {
  load_sample(sample_table$folder[i], sample_table$sample_id[i],
              sample_table$condition[i])
})
names(sample_objects) <- sample_table$sample_id

# Match the sample order and labeling used in the original preparation.
combined <- merge(
  x = sample_objects[[1]],
  y = sample_objects[-1],
  add.cell.ids = sample_table$sample_id,
  project = "7m_snRNAseq"
)
combined[["RNA"]] <- JoinLayers(combined[["RNA"]])

print(table(combined$condition, combined$sample_id))
# Optional: cache the input object locally; it is not necessary to upload it to GitHub.
# saveRDS(combined, file = "7m_snRNAseq_combined.rds")

seurat_list_raw <- SplitObject(combined, split.by = "sample_id")

```

```{r}
## 2. Per-sample quality control

```{r quality-control}
# Mouse mitochondrial genes typically begin with 'mt-'.
seurat_list_raw <- lapply(seurat_list_raw, function(s) {
  s[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(s, pattern = "^mt-")
  s
})

summarize_qc <- function(object_list) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(object_list), function(sid) {
    s <- object_list[[sid]]
    data.frame(
      sample = sid,
      cells = ncol(s),
      med_nFeature = median(s$nFeature_RNA),
      med_nCount = median(s$nCount_RNA),
      med_mt = median(s$percent.mt)
    )
  }))
}

qc_pre <- summarize_qc(seurat_list_raw)
print(qc_pre)

seurat_list_qc <- lapply(seurat_list_raw, function(s) {
  subset(s, subset =
    nFeature_RNA >= 200 &
    nFeature_RNA <= 7000 &
    nCount_RNA >= 500 &
    nCount_RNA <= 50000 &
    percent.mt <= 15
  )
})

qc_post <- summarize_qc(seurat_list_qc)
print(qc_post)

```

```{r}
## 3. Ambient RNA correction using decontX

The `decontX` algorithm was applied separately to each QC-filtered sample,
without an additional empty-droplet background matrix. The decontaminated
count matrix was used downstream. Cells with an estimated contamination
fraction greater than 0.30 were removed.

```{r ambient-rna}
seurat_list_decontx <- lapply(names(seurat_list_qc), function(sid) {
  s <- seurat_list_qc[[sid]]
  orig_counts <- GetAssayData(s, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
  orig_per_cell <- Matrix::colSums(orig_counts)

  sce <- as.SingleCellExperiment(s)
  sce <- celda::decontX(sce)
  decon_counts <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(sce, "decontXcounts")
  new_per_cell <- Matrix::colSums(decon_counts)
  frac_removed <- 1 - (new_per_cell / orig_per_cell[colnames(decon_counts)])

  s2 <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = decon_counts, assay = "RNA", project = sid)
  s2 <- AddMetaData(s2, as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(sce)))
  s2$sample_id <- s$sample_id[colnames(s2)]
  s2$condition <- s$condition[colnames(s2)]
  s2$decontX_frac_removed <- frac_removed[colnames(s2)]

  # Preserve original, uncorrected counts in a separate assay at this stage.
  s2[["RNA_raw"]] <- CreateAssayObject(
    counts = orig_counts[, colnames(s2), drop = FALSE]
  )
  s2 <- subset(s2, subset = decontX_contamination <= 0.30)
  s2
})
names(seurat_list_decontx) <- names(seurat_list_qc)

```

```{r}
## 4. Doublet detection and singlet retention

`scDblFinder` was run separately for each sample after ambient RNA correction.
Only cells classified as singlets were retained. The rebuilt Seurat objects
contain the decontaminated counts; the temporary `RNA_raw` assay from the
previous step is **not** retained after this reconstruction.

```{r doublet-detection}
seurat_list_clean <- lapply(names(seurat_list_decontx), function(sid) {
  s <- seurat_list_decontx[[sid]]
  sce <- as.SingleCellExperiment(s, assay = "RNA")
  sce <- scDblFinder::scDblFinder(sce)
  sce <- sce[, sce$scDblFinder.class == "singlet"]

  s2 <- CreateSeuratObject(
    counts = SummarizedExperiment::assay(sce, "counts"),
    project = sid
  )
  s2 <- AddMetaData(s2, as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(sce)))
  s2$sample_id <- sid
  s2$condition <- unique(s$condition)
  s2
})
names(seurat_list_clean) <- names(seurat_list_decontx)

dbl_stats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(seurat_list_clean), function(sid) {
  data.frame(
    sample = sid,
    before = ncol(seurat_list_decontx[[sid]]),
    after = ncol(seurat_list_clean[[sid]]),
    removed = ncol(seurat_list_decontx[[sid]]) - ncol(seurat_list_clean[[sid]])
  )
}))
print(dbl_stats)
```

```{r}
## 5. Merge samples, normalize, and perform dimensionality reduction

```{r integration-and-clustering}
merged <- merge(
  x = seurat_list_clean[[1]],
  y = seurat_list_clean[-1],
  add.cell.ids = names(seurat_list_clean),
  project = "mouse_7m_snRNA"
)
print(table(merged$condition, merged$sample_id))

# For Seurat v5, joining sample-specific count layers may be necessary before
# normalization.

merged <- NormalizeData(merged, verbose = FALSE)
merged <- FindVariableFeatures(merged, nfeatures = 3000, verbose = FALSE)
vars_regress <- intersect(c("nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"), colnames(merged[[]]))
merged <- ScaleData(merged, vars.to.regress = vars_regress, verbose = FALSE)
merged <- RunPCA(merged, npcs = 50, verbose = FALSE)

merged <- RunHarmony(
  object = merged,
  group.by.vars = "sample_id",
  dims.use = 1:50
)
merged <- RunUMAP(merged, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:20)
merged <- FindNeighbors(merged, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:20)
merged <- FindClusters(merged, resolution = 0.3)

DimPlot(merged, reduction = "umap", group.by = "seurat_clusters",
        label = TRUE, repel = TRUE)
FeaturePlot(merged, features = c("Gfap", "Aqp4", "Aldh1l1", "Slc1a3"),
            raster = TRUE)
```


```{r}
## 6. Select astrocytes and classify CXCL14 expression

Cluster 8 was annotated as astrocytic based on the marker-expression plots in
the original analysis. This cluster number is not a transferable cell-type
identifier for independently rerun clustering.

```{r astrocyte-subsetting}
Idents(merged) <- "seurat_clusters"
astro <- subset(merged, idents = "8")
print(table(astro$condition))
print(astro)

DefaultAssay(astro) <- "RNA"
astro[["RNA"]] <- JoinLayers(astro[["RNA"]])
cnt <- GetAssayData(astro, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
stopifnot("Cxcl14" %in% rownames(cnt))

astro$Cxcl14_pos <- ifelse(
  cnt["Cxcl14", ] > 0,
  "Cxcl14_pos",
  "Cxcl14_neg"
)
print(table(astro$Cxcl14_pos, astro$condition))
print(table(astro$sample_id, astro$Cxcl14_pos))
```

```{r}
## 7. Reactive astrocyte marker expression among CXCL14-positive cells

#Dot size represents the percentage of cells expressing each gene. Dot color
#represents relative average expression rescaled to 0–1 within the displayed
#marker category; **it is not an absolute log-normalized expression value**.

```#
obj <- subset(astro, subset = Cxcl14_pos == "Cxcl14_pos")
group_col <- "condition"
obj@meta.data[[group_col]] <- factor(
  obj@meta.data[[group_col]], levels = c("WT", "5XFAD")
)

genes_list <- list(
  "Reactive astrocyte markers" = c("Gfap", "C4b", "Chil1",
                                  "Lgals3bp", "Stat1", "Stat3")
)
genes_list <- lapply(genes_list, function(g) intersect(g, rownames(obj)))
features <- unlist(genes_list, use.names = FALSE)

gene2cat <- stack(genes_list) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Gene = values, Category = ind)

p <- DotPlot(obj, features = features, group.by = group_col,
             assay = DefaultAssay(obj))
pd <- p$data %>%
  left_join(gene2cat, by = c("features.plot" = "Gene")) %>%
  mutate(
    Category = factor(Category, levels = names(genes_list)),
    features.plot = factor(
      features.plot,
      levels = unlist(lapply(names(genes_list), function(ct) rev(genes_list[[ct]])))
    )
  )

pd_facet <- pd %>%
  group_by(Category) %>%
  mutate(avg_exp_facet_scaled = scales::rescale(avg.exp)) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(pd_facet, aes(x = id, y = features.plot)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = pct.exp, color = avg_exp_facet_scaled)) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(Category), scales = "free_y", space = "free_y",
             switch = "y") +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "Relative average expression") +
  scale_size(range = c(1.5, 7), name = "Percent expressed") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 24, face = "bold"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90", color = NA),
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    strip.placement = "outside",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", color = "black")
  )
```
